name: TLP290(GB-TP,SE
title: AC-input phototransistor photocoupler, 4-pin surface mount
summary: The TLP290 is a single-channel photocoupler for AC or DC input: two GaAs infrared emitters, wired anti-parallel across pins 1 and 2, light a phototransistor on pins 3 and 4, so current of either polarity turns the output on. It is built for input modules of programmable controllers and for hybrid ICs, in a small surface-mount package. The output withstands 80 V, isolation is 3750 Vrms for one minute, operation is specified from -55 to 110 °C, and the transfer ratio is sorted into ranks, GB being 100 to 400 %. The part is marked not recommended for new designs.

circuits.title: Collector current ratio test circuit
circuits.description: Set-up for the collector current ratio. A forward current is forced into pin 1 (IF1) for one reading and into pin 2 (IF2) for the other, so each of the two emitters is lit in turn. The collector is held at VCE = 5 V and the emitter is grounded; IC1 and IC2 are the collector currents for the two directions, and the ratio IC2/IC1 must lie between 0.33 and 3.

circuits.title: Switching time test circuit
circuits.description: Set-up for the switching times. The input current pulse IF enters pin 1 and returns from pin 2 through a series resistor of unstated value to ground. The phototransistor is a common-emitter switch: the emitter is grounded, RL pulls the collector up to VCC, and VCE is read at the collector. The table figures use RL = 1.9 kΩ, VCC = 5 V and IF = ±16 mA.

operation.text: Two infrared emitters sit back to back across pins 1 and 2. Current in one direction lights one, current in the other lights the second, so the phototransistor responds to AC or to DC of either polarity. The collector current ratio for the two directions lies between 0.33 and 3.

The transfer ratio at IF = 5 mA, VCE = 5 V is sorted into ranks: Y 50 to 150 %, GR 100 to 300 %, BLL 200 to 400 %, GB 100 to 400 %; unranked parts cover 50 to 400 % and may carry any of the rank marks. Rank GB also guarantees a saturated ratio of at least 30 % at IF = ±1 mA, VCE = 0.4 V, and VCE(sat) of 0.3 V max at IC = 0.2 mA, IF = ±1 mA.

Input forward current is ±50 mA up to 90 °C and falls by 1.5 mA/°C above that, to 20 mA at 110 °C; input power falls by 3.0 mW/°C above 90 °C. Collector dissipation is 150 mW and total dissipation 200 mW at 25 °C, falling by 1.5 mW/°C and 2.0 mW/°C above 25 °C. Pulsed input current is 1 A for pulses of 100 µs or less at low duty cycle, falling to 50 mA at a duty ratio of 1.

Typical transfer ratio at VCE = 5 V or 10 V rises from about 20 % at 0.1 mA to a broad peak near 200 % around 10 to 20 mA, then falls at higher input current. Collector current at a fixed input peaks between about -20 and 20 °C and drops at high temperature, more steeply at low input current. Dark current rises roughly a decade per 20 °C.

Storage and turn-off times grow with load resistance: at IF = 16 mA and VCC = 5 V, toff is about 40 µs with 1 kΩ and near 1.9 ms with 100 kΩ, while turn-on stays at a few microseconds. Storage and turn-off times lengthen as temperature rises.
Sustained high temperature, current or voltage, or large temperature changes, can reduce reliability substantially even inside the absolute maximum ratings.

Store the parts away from moisture, direct sunlight, corrosive gas and dust, at 5 to 35 °C and 45 to 75 % relative humidity, with little temperature change so that condensation does not oxidise the leads. Keep loads off the parts, use anti-static containers once they are unpacked, and follow the packing label. After more than two years of storage the leads are checked for solderability before use.

The top face carries a pin 1 mark, the type code P290, the CTR rank mark, the lot number, the country of origin (J for Japan) and the process lot number; the V4 option adds a V mark on the part, and its packing carries the VDE mark.
